item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 24, 2026
item.description: AI bubble first: Prof G Markets argues the bubble is not in the stock market (multiples down even as profits rose); AI Daily Brief separates a stock crash from a credit crisis and sizes the neocloud scare; Why X draws the 1973 Nifty Fifty / oil-shock parallel to Huang's 'scarcity of capital'; Rebel Capitalist on why the Cisco analogy fails and financing-inflated chip demand. Supply/demand: Amazon's warehoused GB300 racks are a power problem, not a demand problem; Dan Ives' distinction between demand for compute and the cost of paying for it; FinVid on a compute-constrained world through 2028; BBC on the data-center backlash and Meta + Apple putting open-weight AI on desktop Macs. Watchlist: Micron's Taiwan union vote, YMTC's move into DRAM, and Huang seeing no memory glut by 2029; Ricky Gutierrez on the neocloud/Intel selloff; FinVid on physical AI as Nvidia's next leg.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 23, 2026
item.description: Bubble first: House of El on Anthropic's $80B H1 loss (mostly accounting, but real cash burn: $1.76 spent per $1 earned), Amazon's $92B paper gain on convertible notes, $518B of non-cancellable compute contracts, and CoreWeave's $50B debt the market now prices as troubled. Ed Zitron on the IMF warning, the bond market freaking out, rising CDS on Nvidia/Microsoft/Meta, and 45% of market value in nine companies. Internet Education on circular financing (Nvidia<->OpenAI, Oracle debt) and the capex explosion: Meta $72B to $130-145B, Amazon $128B to $220B. Dividend Talks: Tom Lee's buy case vs negative combined hyperscaler FCF, Meta capex +80% vs revenue +26%, rising default-protection costs. Then the bull pushback: Luke Lango says financing fears are overblown, CoreWeave won't blow up, semis at cheapest valuations. Supply/demand: Jensen Huang at GTC Berlin — neoclouds are a working-capital problem, not a demand problem; no 2029 memory glut. Lango: Anthropic's slowdown is OpenAI's market-share gain; combined ARR growth re-accelerating since July. Ben Horowitz: Jassy says Amazon is 'out of everything' beyond 2028; the world stays compute-constrained at least through 2028. Watchlist: Lam Research guided slightly above consensus and would have guided higher without supply-chain constraints (demand too strong). And Huang's bearish counterpoint on memory: Nvidia is 'open-minded' to Chinese suppliers (CXMT), a direct read-across for Micron.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 22, 2026
item.description: Bubble: Ed Zitron (Dot Plot) — OpenAI's $750B compute spend through 2030, private capital exhausted, Anthropic's $400B+ in non-cancellable compute deals; Zitron (Tech Report) — where is the money going when tens of billions a quarter yield few million of GPUs; JayzTwoCents on the Open Markets Institute 'Brace for Impact' report — debt, circular money, AI-debt repackaged into pensions and endowments. Supply/demand: Ross Givens — Anthropic's $518B in committed compute (~8 years of revenue), OpenAI's ~$1.4T, 'promised to buy chips as if the boom never ends'; SMCI's $18.5-19.5B guide raise, SpaceX's neocloud-led revenue and its $920M contract for 110K GPUs; MS NOW — the power race: Virginia data centers at 39% of state energy, US demand 80GW→150GW by 2028, 'a race to find power.' Watchlist: the selloff — NVDA -4.4% ($212.21), AMD -8.1%, SK Hynix US -8.07%, MRVL -8%+, INTC -8.04%, SOX -6% on three messages (Meta funding, Tesla trim, Lam speed limit); Nvidia's Vera CPU for the agent era, Mercedes extended self-driving pact, BNP Paribas Ackerman to $345; TSM +68.7% profit surge, LRCX $200B+ WFE and $2.5B Aether target; Broadcom at $326, ~10x since 2022, $300 support, VMware overhang.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 20, 2026
item.description: Bubble: Stoic Finance on the Ellis AI IPO crashing 32% on day one, neocloud financing fears, CoreWeave bond yields at 15%; InvestorPlace debate — Eric says the AI trade is long in the tooth, an asymmetrical trade, broad market topped in August; Market Signal — 10 companies carry 68% of S&P Q3 earnings growth (Goldman), cheap multiples rest on huge forecasts, Piper's $300 Nvidia target at 14x 2028 earnings. Davidson) — Anthropic growth slowdown doesn't matter, profit pools accrue to NVDA/Broadcom/Micron/AMD; FinVid news — Nvidia asks Samsung/SK Hynix/Micron for NVHBM base dies on TSMC 3nm, Microsoft UK data center pullout over power delays (23K GPUs), Anthropic $45B compute deal doubling, Micron Taiwan strike vote and $33B buyback; Dan Ives — Nvidia numbers underestimated 25-30%, Asia checks accelerating; Jose Najarro — Meta's 1M-GPU supercluster, GB300 reliability gains, power the binding bottleneck (170kW racks).
